advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the push-leg transport retry with the `_MAX_RETRIES` loop so transport retries either do not advance `attempt` or the comment claiming budget isolation is corrected to match the actual shared-loop behavior.
evidence: push.py:520-522: '# Bug f61c: transport attempts are counted SEPARATELY from the non-fast-forward budget / # so a blip cannot silently consume the merge-recovery retries the non-FF path needs. / transport_attempts = 1'

push.py:549-551: 'if _retry_transport_or_stop(...):\n    transport_attempts += 1\n    continue' — the continue advances `attempt`, spending a slot of the shared _MAX_RETRIES loop that the non-FF path (_recover_non_fast_forward) also draws from

The separate `transport_attempts` counter only bounds transport retries at _MAX_TRANSPORT_ATTEMPTS via the guard in _retry_transport_or_stop (push_classify.py:209); it does not stop the outer loop counter from advancing, so if a transport blip is followed by non-FF rejections the non-FF path gets fewer than _MAX_RETRIES recovery cycles.
advisory.finding: The push-leg transport retry advances the shared `for attempt in range(1, _MAX_RETRIES + 1)` loop via `continue`, so a transport blip DOES consume a non-fast-forward recovery iteration — contradicting the inline comment that the separate `transport_attempts` counter prevents a blip from consuming the merge-recovery budget.
scenarios: A push attempt fails with a transient TLS/DNS fault (transport retry, attempt advances), the retried push then hits genuine non-fast-forward rejections repeatedly — the non-FF fetch+merge recovery now has fewer than 5 iterations before 'final-push-rejected'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives `_fetch_for_recovery` through a transient transport fault (retry-then-succeed) and a persistent one (bounded stop with push-transport-failed), asserting fetch call count and backoff.
evidence: push.py:313-337 defines `_fetch_for_recovery` with its own `for transport_attempt in range(1, _MAX_TRANSPORT_ATTEMPTS + 1)` retry loop, `_is_transport_retriable` check, and `_transport_backoff` call

In tests/unit/test_push_strict.py the `_recovery_git` helper (lines 383-407) and `_non_ff_git` (lines 169-190) have no `fetch` branch, so a `fetch` call returns the default `_completed(args)` with rc=0 (success) — the fetch never fails in any test

advisory.finding: The new fetch-leg transport retry (_fetch_for_recovery) has no test: no test makes a `git fetch` return a transient transport fault, so its retry/backoff/bounded-budget/terminal-reason behavior is entirely unexercised even though the commit message attributes run 31420498173's lost merge recovery to this exact leg.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend `_recovery_git` with a `fetch_results: list[tuple[int, str]]` branch and add tests mirroring the push-leg pair: one where fetch fails with _CI_TLS_STDERR once then succeeds (assert fetch called twice, one backoff), and one where fetch fails _MAX_TRANSPORT_ATTEMPTS times (assert bounded stop and terminal reason).

evidence: push.py:256 `_git(base_path, "merge", "--abort")` runs before each transport-retry backoff
tests/unit/test_push_strict.py:437 filters out abort calls: `merges = [c for c in calls if c and c[0] == "merge" and c[1:2] != ("--abort",)]` and only asserts `len(merges) == 2`
No assertion in either merge-recovery test checks that a `merge --abort` occurred between the failed and retried merge
advisory.finding: test_merge_recovery_retries_a_promisor_transport_fault asserts the retried merge count but never verifies the `git merge --abort` that the recovery contract performs between attempts (push.py:256), leaving that introduced cleanup side-effect unasserted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert ('merge', '--abort') in calls` (or count aborts == retries) to the transport-fault merge-recovery test.
